# Sector — agent1’s player review

- Original source: [Robin Hood](https://www.sector.sk/uzivatelrecenzia/1360/robin-hood.htm)
- Author / publication: agent1; Sector.sk.
- Language / date: Slovak; 2007-02-21.
- Access: Full user review retrieved directly
- Checked: 2026-09-09
- Retrieved: 2026-09-09
- Archived copy: lookup failed (archive.org rate limit); not checked
- Format: header notes, original summary, then complete factual notes (user review on a commercial site, not transcribed)

Scoring the game 9.0, agent1 praises its detailed graphics, music, modest hardware demands, and Czech voice acting. The account covers campaign profiles, difficulty selection, forest ambushes, character abilities, and camp assignments for gathering supplies, manufacturing equipment, and training.

The author finds some items unnecessary in practice and considers moving large numbers of bodies tedious. Mouse-drawn combat gestures and the recruitment incentive for avoiding kills receive particular attention. The reported experience is with the Czech edition; the hardware anecdote is evidence of one player’s experience, not a formal minimum specification or a current compatibility test.

## Detailed notes

Page facts: user review "Robin Hood" (platform PC) in Sector.sk's "používateľské recenzie" (user reviews); "pridal agent1 21.2.2007 o 14:07"; score 9.0 (site's 10-point scale); signed "napísal agent1 21.2.2007"; no comment count shown (commenting requires login); retrieved directly from sector.sk. Slovak user review on a commercial site, not transcribed.

Content, in order:

- Legend recap: Robin robbed the rich and gave to the poor, hiding in Sherwood with his band and ambushing nobles crossing the forest; King Richard the Lionheart left for a crusade to Jerusalem; Prince John seized the throne and, with the Sheriff of Nottingham, oppresses the people with "un-Christian taxes".
- Intro cinematic, as the reviewer describes it: after the Spellbound logo, soldiers led by a sergeant who is also tax collector burst into a peasant home while a peasant boy watches through barn boards; the peasant woman begs; Robin's arrow pins the money bag from the sergeant's hand to a door; the sergeant sends soldiers after Robin, who handles them and forces the sergeant to return the bag; the peasant says the Sheriff will never give up; Robin shoots an arrow into the air saying King Richard will return before it touches the ground.
- Main menu: dominated by green with a castle in the background and atmospheric music. First step is creating a player profile, which then records data such as percentage of the game completed and money on account. Menu items: Settings, Authors (credits), Load game, Play movies (intro and outro), Exit, and Play. On first Play with a profile the game asks for a difficulty: higher difficulty gives enemies more health and attack; even on Easy some parts must be repeated.
- Missions: "around 40 different missions"; the reviewer liked the first one best. Settings: five castles (Lincoln, Nottingham, Leicester, Derby, York) and three locations in Sherwood Forest. Goal: gather the ransom for King Richard, who the player learns has been captured. Forest missions are described as the best earners.
- Camp: a hideout in Sherwood with dwellings where useful items are made, e.g. nets, arrows, healing herbs; stones come from the river and apples from trees. Many such items exist; the reviewer admits not using some. Soldiers can be sent to train in close combat or archery.
- Forest mission types: robbing a tax collector, robbing a coach with valuables, or freeing homesteads attacked by the Sheriff's soldiers. In one such homestead Little John joins.
- Main characters listed: Lady Marian (Robin's love); Friar Tuck ("Marian's fat priest", originally at Nottingham church); Will Scarlet (Robin's cousin, skilled with a mace); Stuteley (Robin's good friend). Abilities: Robin shoots the bow, knocks enemies out with a fist punch, and can rob enemies of valuables; Stuteley disguises as a beggar and throws nets and apples; large characters such as Little John can carry a body (dead or stunned) out of sight, important to avoid alarms. The reviewer sometimes played "kill everything that moves", when hiding two dozen corpses becomes pointless.
- Townspeople cannot be killed, only stunned ("what a pity"), and when they spot the player they run screaming to alert guards.
- Guard vision is checked through an icon in the top-right corner; when a guard's view field turns red they have spotted you (and you probably hear the shout).
- Combat gestures: holding the mouse button and drawing a shape; a straight line makes Robin lunge straight with the sword; a horizontal figure-eight performs a special strike an ordinary mortal usually does not survive.
- Advice: avoid killing when possible; the game becomes more interesting, and at the end of each mission the game reports how many people joined the band, more the fewer enemies killed.
- Four-leaf clover: pick it up; if a hero is killed they soon jump back up ready to fight; the clover is consumed.
- Party overview via small parchments at the bottom of the screen, one per hero, showing health and abilities.
- Technical: graphics very successful and detailed, likewise the in-game videos; sounds "not the worst"; the reviewer has the Czech version and finds the CD Projekt dubbing well done, especially the soldiers' occasional lines. Resolutions offered: 640x480, 800x600, 1024x768; the middle one recommended. Hardware demands are low: ran fine on 64MB RAM, 500 MHz, 32MB GPU.
- Pluses: detailed graphics; low hardware requirements; good music. Minuses: some items are theoretically useless; clearing away large numbers of bodies is sometimes lengthy and tiring.
